sources.title: Adam Neumann gets $1.7 billion to leave WeWork

claims.claim: WeWork reached a peak private valuation of $47 billion in 2019.
The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in November 2023.
Co-founder Adam Neumann walked away with a payout of roughly $1.7 billion when forced out.

scenes.narration: How do you burn forty-seven billion dollars in four years? You convince the world a real estate company is a tech startup.

visual.headline: The fastest wealth incineration in history.

visualAssets.editorialPurpose: Gedung perkantoran modern kaca - merepresentasikan ilusi kerajaan real estate

scenes.narration: Founder Adam Neumann didn't sell desks. He sold a movement. His stated mission wasn't to rent offices, but to elevate the world's consciousness.

visual.quote: Our mission is to elevate the world's consciousness.

scenes.narration: The reality was simple arbitrage. Sign expensive long-term leases, and rent them out short-term. In 2019: valued at 47 billion. By 2023: Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

visual.subtitle: The fatal flaw of long-term liabilities and short-term revenue.

scenes.narration: But the founder didn't sink with the ship. When Neumann was forced out, he walked away with a golden parachute worth one point seven billion.

visual.label: Payout to Adam Neumann
visual.subtitle: The company collapsed. The founder became a billionaire.

scenes.narration: The WeWork playbook: Use venture capital to subsidize losses. Grow relentlessly. Ignore unit economics. Disguise real estate as a tech platform.

visual.headline: Growth at the cost of survival.

scenes.narration: Charisma can raise billions, but it can't fix a broken business model. Mathematics always wins in the end.

visual.question: ARE YOUR ECONOMICS SOUND?
visual.subtitle: A broken model doesn't scale. It just crashes harder.

packaging.youtubeTitle: How WeWork Burned $47 Billion in 4 Years (The Flawed Strategy)
packaging.instagramCaption:
The $47 Billion Illusion. 🏢📉

How do you burn billions in venture capital? Convince the world a real estate company is a tech startup. WeWork reached a $47B valuation in 2019 by ignoring unit economics and prioritizing relentless growth. By 2023, they filed for bankruptcy.

The fatal flaw? Arbitrage. Signing long-term leases while collecting short-term rent.

The crazy part? Founder Adam Neumann walked away with a $1.7 billion payout while the company crashed.

Charisma raises money. But mathematics always wins.

Sources: WSJ, CNBC
